newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen steady to easier in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen steady to easier in thin trade.

text.p: The dollar is expected to be steady to slightly easier on Friday, with trade subdued ahead of Easter holidays in Europe and the United States, dealers said.
But the yen's continuing weakness versus the mark in cross trade may indirectly support the dollar/yen rate, joined by steady bids from Japanese investors near and below 123 yen, they added.
In what is expected to be a thin market, traders will be wary about possible remarks by monetary officials on currencies and any speculative moves that may make rates fluctuate widely.

On the topside, the dollar's fall against the mark overnight could weigh on the dollar versus the yen if speculative selling on technical factors keeps pressuring dollar/mark rates in Asia, dealers said.
"If the dollar falls below 1.6700 marks, a key support point, a dive below 123 yen would be possible," said a trust bank dealer.

Dealers said the dollar's topside remains heavy as the market remains cautious about any possible expression of concern from officials over Japan-U.S. trade friction after Thursday's comments by Deputy Treasury Secretary Summers.

Summers said on Thursday in a television talk show in New York: "We have been expressing concerns for some time about Japan and about the dangerous possibility that the Japanese current account surplus would expand substantially."

While traders are wary of possible speculative dollar selling for marks and yen, the yen's weakness against the mark in cross trade is expected to prevent the dollar from falling sharply against the yen, dealers said. The mark rose above a key resistance point of 73.80 yen overnight.
Japanese investors' buying interest on falls will also help support the dollar near 123.20 yen, they added.
